title: I’ve spent almost a year making my first game, and I’m honestly terrified of releasing it.
author: Apprehensive-Apple52
selftext:
Hey everyone

My game, **Stickville**, is releasing to Steam on October 27, and with the Steam fest event coming up, I realized I’ve barely told anyone about it.

I’m a solo developer, and I’ve spent roughly 9–10 months working on this game. I’m not a professional programmer or artist, and I’ve relied heavily on AI to help me create things I wouldn’t have been able to make on my own.

I know AI in games is controversial, and I understand that not everyone will be interested in a game made this way. I’m not going to pretend I made everything by hand.

**But I’ve put so much time, frustration, learning and care into this project.**

Even with AI, getting everything to work and slowly turning an idea into an actual game has been a much bigger challenge than I ever expected.

And honestly, **I’m really proud of what I’ve managed to create.**

Stickville is a little exploration game where you can wander around, discover things and simply enjoy spending time in the world.

I’m not expecting to become the next big indie success story. I know how crowded Steam is, and I know my game won’t be for everyone.  
But I still remember getting a genuinely kind comment about my game *once*. **It made me ridiculously happy.**

It’s hard to explain, but knowing that someone enjoyed something I had spent so much time creating made the whole process feel worth it.  
**I guess I’m hoping to give someone else that feeling, too.**

I’ve been pretty terrible at marketing the game, and putting myself out there like this feels a little scary. But I figured I should at least give it a chance instead of quietly releasing it and hoping someone happens to find it.

If you feel like checking out Stickville, you can find it on Steam here:  
[**https://store.steampowered.com/app/4805960/Stickville/**](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4805960/Stickville/)

The game releases on **October 27**, and I’d genuinely appreciate anyone taking a look. Thanks for reading, and good luck to everyone else working on their own games! ❤️

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: As long as you enjoyed the process that is all thst matters, if building it was bringing you joy and not just doing it for the profit then any purchase of the game might make it seem like a nice bonus 🙂

Still I hope you get what you're hoping for out of the game.
